title: Is it possible to turn on convert mode after import?
description:
I have a Python object that extends a Dict, but also provides some additional functions, which return basic items like strings.

Right now if you use `reticulate::import(..., convert=TRUE)`, when I create this object, I end up with an R list, which lacks the 'extra functions' that were attached to the python object. This is because reticulate detects that object as a `Dict` and automatically converts it.

So, I use `convert=FALSE`, and then I can access the extra function with `object$function(...)` -- however, I'd like the return of these functions to be automatically converted.

So, what I want auto-conversion to be *off* for the initial object creation, so I get the full python object, but then I want to *turn on* the automatic conversion so that from that object, the function results are all converted.

Is this possible? Here is some code that demonstrates what I mean. If I use `convert=TRUE`, then I lack the `seek` function on my `RefGenConf` object:


```
> mod = reticulate::import("refgenconf", convert=TRUE)
> rgc1 = mod$RefGenConf(Sys.getenv("REFGENIE"))
> class(rgc1)
[1] "list"
> rgc1$seek("t7", "fasta")
Error: attempt to apply non-function
```

But if I use `convert=FALSE`, the function return Python objects instead of R objects by default:

```
> mod = reticulate::import("refgenconf", convert=FALSE)
> rgc2 = mod$RefGenConf(Sys.getenv("REFGENIE"))
> class(rgc2)
 [1] "refgenconf.refgenconf.RefGenConf"  "yacman.yacman.YacAttMap"

[1] "/home/nsheff/code/refgenie_sandbox/t7/fasta/default/t7.fa"

I know I can just wrap everything in `py_to_r`, but what I'd like is the happy medium: a function like `rgc$set_convert(TRUE)` so that later functions will now automatically wrap results.

title: GPU memory leakage when creating objects from sentence-transformers
description:
# **Description**
I am creating a function in R that embeds sentences using the `sentence_transformers` library from Python. 

For some unknown reason, creating the object multiple times under the same variable name ends up in insufficient memory space to allocate the transformer. To reproduce:

```{r}
sentence_transformers <- reticulate::import("sentence_transformers")
for (i in 1:10) {
  print(i)
  bert_encoder <- sentence_transformers$SentenceTransformer("bert-large-nli-stsb-mean-tokens")
}
```
However, doing the same operation directly on Python does not produce an error
```{Python}
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
for i in range(10):
    print(i)
    bert_encoder = SentenceTransformer("bert-large-nli-stsb-mean-tokens")
}
```
This happens with any model that is allocated in GPU. On my NVIDIA GTX 1060 it reaches the 4th cycle, but on smaller GPUs it crashes earlier. One temporal solution is to create the model outside only once, and then pass the model as a parameter to the function as many times as wanted, but I would rather avoid that because it adds an extra step and in any case calling multiple models might just make it crash as well.

# **Expected behaviour**
The for loop finishes without an error

# **Observed behaviour**
_Error in py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords) : 
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 20.00 MiB (GPU 0; 6.00 GiB total capacity; 2.95 GiB already allocated; 16.11 MiB free; 238.68 MiB cached)_ 

# **Unsuccesful attemps at solving it**

1. The solutions proposed [here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/36465)
2. Using numba as suggested [here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/60354785/5559413)
3. Declaring the variable explicitely on Python via `reticulate::py_run_string()` and then doing `del bert_encoder` and calling the garbage collector

# **Details**
Windows 10 Home
Python 3.7.4
R 4.0.1
Reticulate 1.16
Torch 1.3.1
Tensorflow 2.2.0
Transformers 2.11.0
sentence_transformers 0.2.6

title: Virtualenvs are hard-coded to be created with the --system-site-packages flag
description:
I have an issue with a shinyapps.io application that is no longer able to pip install packages using reticulate. The error I am seeing in the logs is ```ImportError: No module named 'setuptools.build_meta'``` 

I believe it is a result of this open issue with pip: https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6264 (Some additional helpful information is provided here by the setuptools maintainers: https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/1694#issuecomment-466010982) 

The application is running on an older version of Ubuntu (Xenial) which ships with older versions of system python packages such as setuptools: https://packages.ubuntu.com/xenial/python-setuptools

Because the reticulate virtualenv is always created with the --system-site-packages flag, the user cannot opt out of including system packages even when running in virtualized environments such as shinyapps.io where they do not have control over the system. 

https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/a8701771fe759161c76a8e4a81d4ccc506269de1/R/virtualenv.R#L79

It seems as though this flag should not be set since it breaks the isolation from the system packages or it should at least be an optional argument.

title: Use own Conda environment on an R package
description:
Hi, I'm developing an R package ([deepredeff](https://github.com/ruthkr/deepredeff)) that uses the `keras` and `tensorflow` R packages. I've followed the [Managing an R Package’s Python Dependencies](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/reticulate/vignettes/python_dependencies.html) to set the `Config/reticulate:` section on the `DESCRIPTION` file as well as the `.onLoad()` function.

### Issue

The package works as expected if the user uses the autoconfiguration from `reticulate::configure_environment()` (i.e., using the `r-reticulate` environment on Miniconda). However, I would also give the option to use an existing TensorFlow installation if the user already has it installed on their system.

The problem is that I get the following error when using `reticulate::use_condaenv()`:
``` r
library(deepredeff)
reticulate::use_condaenv("tensorflow", conda = "/usr/local/Caskroom/miniconda/base/bin/conda")
reticulate::conda_binary()
#> [1] "/usr/local/Caskroom/miniconda/base/bin/conda"
reticulate::repl_python()
#> Error: Specified conda binary '/Users/ruth/Library/r-miniconda/bin/conda' does not exist.
```

If I run `repl_python()` again (on the same session), somehow it's able to locate the Conda environment specified earlier:

```r
reticulate::repl_python()
#> Python 3.7.5 (/usr/local/Caskroom/miniconda/base/envs/tensorflow/bin/python)
#> Reticulate 1.16 REPL -- A Python interpreter in R.
#> exit
```

#### Note
This issue only happens if `library(deepredeff)` is loaded at the beginning. Without, reticulate never tries to load the `r-reticulate` environment.

#### More details

Actually, I found this issue when trying to run my `predict_effector()` function on my preexisting Conda installation. The first time it's run it gives an Error, and I if I run it again, it successfully runs on my specified Conda environment without issues.
```r
pred_result <- deepredeff::predict_effector(
  input = bacteria_fasta_path,
  taxon = "bacteria"
)
># WARNING: incompatible requirements for package 'tensorflow' detected!

># WARNING: tensorflow [2.0.0] will be used.

pred_result <- deepredeff::predict_effector(
  input = bacteria_fasta_path,
  taxon = "bacteria"
)
># 2020-07-06 10:48:16.407641: I tensorflow/core/platform/cpu_feature_guard.cc:145] This TensorFlow binary is optimized with Intel(R) MKL-DNN to use the following CPU instructions in performance critical operations:  SSE4.1 SSE4.2 AVX AVX2 FMA

### Questions

- Is there anything wrong or that I can change on my `Config/reticulate:` section or my `.onLoad()` function?

title: Autoconfigure when the same package has multiple names
description:
TensorFlow has now 3 pip packages: `tensorflow-cpu`, `tensorflow` and `tensorflow-gpu`. In theory, the `tensorflow` package should work on both, cpu and gpu systems, but this doesn't seem to be the case for some users. (eg https://github.com/rstudio/keras/issues/1079 )

As we have the autoconfigure enabled for tensorflow in the [DESCRIPTION](https://github.com/rstudio/tensorflow/blob/master/DESCRIPTION#L55-L60) file, we are trying to install `tensorflow` over an over even if the user has already installed `tensorflow-cpu`.

Is there a way to currently handle this?

I wonder if we could have something like:

```
Config/reticulate:
  list(
    packages = list(
      list(package = c("tensorflow", pip = TRUE, alternatives = c("tensorflow-cpu", "tensorflow-gpu"))
    )
  )
```

That would check the alternatives too, before trying to auto install.

title: Export a conda environment as a yaml and import from it
description:
One can export a conda environment as a yaml

```bash
conda activate my_conda
conda env export > my_conda.yaml
```

and then import from it to create a new conda environment

```bash
conda env create -f my_conda.yaml
```

(optionally with -n and -p to bypass the envname and path inscribed in the yaml)

This feature makes a lot of sense for reproducible analysis and could be a part of reticulate, namely: `conda_create` (add a `file` argument) etc. Maybe a new function `conda_export` makes sense too.

If someone seconds it, I would make a pull request.

I'm using knitr and reticulate to render R and python code chunks in a (shiny) website. Works great!

When I do this with python code, chunks the `r.` environment works as expected and is environment specific (see use of `r.x1` in `chunk2` below). However, once you assign something to a variable in any python code chunk, that variable is available in all subsequent python code chunks. 

Sharing (python) environments/namespaces is useful but is there also a way to separate them if needed? Specifically, in the example below it would be great if `chunk2` printed `object 'x1' not found` twice

An extension of the below would be that both `env1` and `env2` have the same parent environment (e.g., `env0`) but python objects created in `env1` or `env2` should "contaminate" the other environments.

    library(reticulate)

    env1$x1 <- "x1"
    env2 <- new.env()
    
    chunk1 <- "
    ```{python echo = FALSE}
    x1 = r.x1
    print(x1)
    ```
    "
    
    chunk2 <- "
    ```{python echo = FALSE}
    print(r.x1)
    print(x1)
    ```
    "
    
    output <- knitr::knit(text = chunk1, quiet = TRUE, envir = env1)
    cat(output)
    output <- knitr::knit(text = chunk2, quiet = TRUE, envir = env2)

title: Automatic r_to_py conversion fails on {arrow} objects
description:
I'm working on a [vignette](https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/ff1f58c9a38d4f5d12963bbda82ef37262f30231/r/vignettes/python.Rmd) for the `arrow` package to document its [new `reticulate` support](https://github.com/apache/arrow/blob/master/r/R/py-to-r.R) for passing data to/from Python with `pyarrow`. In the process, I observed some unexpected behavior.

1. While the automatic `r_to_py` conversion works for regular R objects, it seems to fail for Arrow objects (R6 classes that hold an externalptr). Assuming `arrow` and `pyarrow` as described in that vignette (you need the nightly version of both packages as this is not yet released), this first part works as expected:

```r
pa <- import("pyarrow")
a <- pa$array(c(1, 2, 3))
a

## Array
## <double>
## [
##   1,
##   2,
##   3
## ]
```

I created an Arrow Array using `pyarrow`, passing an R `numeric` vector that gets automatically translated to Python, and because I did `import()` with the default `convert = TRUE`, the result is an R Arrow Array, as if I had made it directly with the R package. All good here.

But if the inputs to the Python function are an Arrow R6 class object, wrapping a C++ pointer, they don't get automatically converted with `r_to_py`. 

```r
# Creating arrays using the R package
a <- Array$create(c(1, 2, 3))
b <- Array$create(c(6, 7, 8))
# Now call a function in pyarrow
pa$concat_arrays(list(a, b))

## Error in py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords) : 
##   Unable to access object (object is from previous session and is now invalid)
```

However, if I explicitly wrap the function input in `r_to_py`, it works:

```r
pa$concat_arrays(r_to_py(list(a, b)))

## Array
## <double>
## [
##   1,
##   2,
##   3,
##   6,
##   7,
##   8
## ]
```

2. If I import with `convert = FALSE`, which I understood to only affect the `py_to_r` behavior, now the automatic `r_to_py` works.

```r
# (in a fresh session)
pa <- import("pyarrow", convert = FALSE)
a <- Array$create(c(1, 2, 3))
b <- Array$create(c(6, 7, 8))
pa$concat_arrays(list(a, b))

## [
##   1,
##   2,
##   3,
##   6,
##   7,
##   8
## ]
```

I'm not very familiar with the internals of `reticulate`, but if I had to guess, I wonder if the code that's inspecting the function inputs sees the Arrow externalptrs, sees that they don't map onto any Python objects from this R session, and assumes that they're stale Python refs.

title: No plot from python plotting function
description:
Hi,

I am trying to plot some matrices with the following python function in Rmarkdown:

```
import os
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

def plot_freq_bin_mats(subject, freq_bins):
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(8,8))
    for i, f in enumerate(freq_bins, start=1):
        subj_file = base_dir + subject + '_' + f + '.txt'
        print(subj_file)
        if os.path.exists(subj_file):
            freq_mat = np.loadtxt(subj_file, delimiter=',')
        else:
            freq_mat = np.zeros((46,46))
        ax = fig.add_subplot(3,4,i)
        ax.set_title("{0}".format(f))
        ax.spy(freq_mat, markersize=1, color='black')
        ax.set_yticks([])
        ax.set_xticks([])
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.suptitle("{0}".format(subject), fontsize=14, y=1)
    plt.show()
```

When I call the function from a python cell, it works as expected, but if I source it in an R cell and try to call it, I get no error but the plot does not show up. Here is the R code I am trying to use:
```
source_python('/path/to/plotting/plot_freq_bins_mat.py')
plot_freq_bin_mats(py$all_subjects[1], py$freq_bins)
```

And here is my r setup:
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::knit_engines$set(python=reticulate::eng_python)
library(reticulate)
use_python('/opt/anaconda3/bin/python')
matplotlib <- import("matplotlib")
matplotlib$use("Agg", force = TRUE)
```
I have tried it with and without the last two lines.

Is there a way to get the plots to work with the R cell block? 

Thanks

title: pandas datetime64[ns] columns with NA-values crash R
description:
Hi,

Creating a pandas DataFrame with a `datetime64` column that contains NA-values, results in a crash of R ("R Session Error: The previous R session was abnormally terminated due to an unexpected crash"):

```{r}
library(reticulate)
pd <- import("pandas")
pd$DataFrame(dict(a = c(1577836800000000000, 1577836900000000000, NA)), dtype = "datetime64[ns]")
```

The same works for any other `dtype`, or for a data without NA-values.

I'm using
```
> sessionInfo()
R version 3.6.0 (2019-04-26)
Platform: x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server 7.6 (Maipo)
```

with
```
> packageVersion("reticulate")
[1] ‘1.14’
```
and pandas version
```
> py_get_attr(pd, "__version__")
1.0.2
```

title: Perform automated sys.stdout.flush() during loops
description:
Console output created during a loop is currently printed to the console only after execution finished. As I recently found out, a manual workaround for this would be to manually add `sys.stdout.flush()` to the loop body (code copied from [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60736401/reticulate-doesnt-print-to-console-in-real-time)), which then creates console output in real time.

```r
library(reticulate)

py_run_string("
import time
from sys import stdout

for i in range(5):
   print(str(i))
   time.sleep(1.5) # sleep for 1.5 sec
   stdout.flush()
")
```

Would it be feasible to integrate this approach natively in **reticulate**?

title: Feature Request: pass pip options through `py_install`
description:
I would really like to see `pip` options can be passed through `py_install`. More specifically, I am interested in the `--install-option` option that will be passed to `setup.py`.

```
  --install-option <options>  Extra arguments to be supplied to the setup.py install command (use
                              like --install-option="--install-scripts=/usr/local/bin"). Use
                              multiple --install-option options to pass multiple options to
                              setup.py install. If you are using an option with a directory path,
                              be sure to use absolute path.
```

It seems that it would be easy to implement an option `pip_options` for `py_install` which accepts a character vector that will be passed to `pip` (if pip is used for installation).

title: winbuilder's note on namespaces
description:
Hello reticulate -

I maintain a package that uses reticulate to offer an optional feature, [here](https://github.com/tkonopka/umap/blob/master/R/umap.R). This works great for me, but recently started giving a 'note' through cran's winbuilder service.

title: Avoid displaying all intermediate outputs in Rmd
description:
The knitr engine displays all results, not just `stdout` or plots, for all lines. This is surprising because sometimes functions return values for convenience, and it's perfectly valid not to use that result if you don't need it. A real example is the sklearn `fit` function, which returns `self` just to permit easy initialization. Example (taken almost verbatim from some course materials I'm writing):

```{python}
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
cv = CountVectorizer(analyzer="char")
docs = ["aaa", "ccc", "abc"]
cv.fit(docs)
cv.transform(docs).A
```

When knit, the chunk splits between `fit` and `transform`, interspersing a useless `CountVectorizer(...)` repr. When run as a single chunk, the two outputs appear in sequence.

I was expecting the behavior of Jupyter Notebook:

* Intermediate values are not displayed by default, but can be displayed by wrapping the result in `display` (or `print`).
* Final values are displayed by default but can be suppressed by adding a `;` at the end of the line.

Perhaps you don't want that exact behavior because R works somewhat differently, but at least it would be nice to have some way of suppressing intermediate outputs (e.g., the trailing `;`, which is the first thing I'd tried).

It looks like this might entail some changes here: https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/master/R/knitr-engine.R#L142

title: Feature request: Automatically convert rounded float arguments to integers.
description:
I found that in this bit of python 
```
# Within python script
data.loc[step_slice, 'cluster'] = OPTICS(
    min_samples = min_samples,
    eps = eps, 
    metric = 'precomputed').fit(distances).labels_
```
I need to cast this argument as an integer: `min_samples = int(min_samples)` to avoid the following error:
```
# Within R script
cols <- c('id', 'type', 'x', 'y', 'z', 'ix', 'iy', 'iz')
header_size <- 9
count_pos <- 4
eps <- 3.5
min_samples <- 2
timestep_ids <- "from_file"

dimensions <- rep(5.3258439000000003e+01, 3)
multicluster <- TRUE

# Calls the python script
if (multicluster) {
  my_python_script(dump_path, csv_path, der_path, 
                 dimensions = dimensions, 
                 timestep_ids = timestep_ids,
                 multicluster = multicluster, 
                 eps = eps, 
                 min_samples = min_samples)
}
```
```
Error in py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords) : 
  TypeError: n_neighbors does not take <class 'float'> value, enter integer value

Detailed traceback: 
  File "<string>", line 185, in my_python_script
  File "C:\...\anaconda3\lib\site-packages\sklearn\cluster\optics_.py", line 248, in fit
    max_eps=self.max_eps)
  File "C:\...\anaconda3\lib\site-packages\sklearn\cluster\optics_.py", line 456, in compute_optics_graph
    nbrs.fit(X)
  File "C:\...\anaconda3\lib\site-packages\sklearn\neighbors\base.py", line 930, in fit
    return self._fit(X)
  File "C:\...\anaconda3\lib\site-packages\sklearn\neighbors\base.py", line 275, in _fit
    type(self.n_neighbors))
```
I realize this is because the value for `min_samples` is being read by python as `2.0`. (`typeof(min_samples)` will print "double") Another solution is to use `as.integer()` in R before passing it to python.

I wonder if automatically converting round value float arguments to integers would be beneficial.
There may be times we specifically want to use the float version of "2". Perhaps this could be an option that you can enable/disable in Reticulate.

title: Module alias isn't recognized inside nested purrr map loop
description:
## The problem Module aliases in the global? environment aren't propagating through the my `purrr::map2` loop. I've started at the core of the nested loop and at every level the sklearn alias is recognized. Only at the outermost layer does it fail. Other reticulate functions such as `r_to_py` don't seem to have this problem. When I place the `import` inside the model function, `sklearn_rf_FUN`, itself, it works.There doesn't seem to be any speed costs associated with putting the `import` inside the model function even though it's repeatedly being called. I've also tried executing the `import` both inside and outside, and it's actually faster when NOT having it on the outside of the model function. Although I only benchmarked it a couple times. It's an easy fix and there doesn't seem to be a cost, but I thought it was odd and may have consequences elsewhere. ## Reproducible example ``` r pacman::p_load(tidymodels, data.table, dtplyr, dplyr, furrr, reticulate) sklearn_e <- import("sklearn.ensemble") # import("sklearn.ensemble", as = "sklearn_e") plan(multiprocess) set.seed(2019) # simulated data; generates 10 multi-patterned, numeric predictors plus outcome variable sim_data <- function(n) { tmp <- mlbench::mlbench.friedman1(n, sd=1) tmp <- cbind(tmp$x, tmp$y) tmp <- as.data.frame(tmp) names(tmp)[ncol(tmp)] <- "y" tmp } # Use small data to tune and compare models small_dat <- sim_data(100) ncv_dat_2 <- nested_cv(small_dat, outside = vfold_cv(v = 2, repeats = 2), inside = bootstraps(times = 2)) error_FUN <- function(y_obs, y_hat){ y_obs <- unlist(y_obs) y_hat <- unlist(y_hat) Metrics::mae(y_obs, y_hat) } sklearn_rf_FUN <- function(params, analysis_set) { # sklearn_e <- import("sklearn.ensemble") max_features <- r_to_py(params$mtry[[1]]) n_estimators <- r_to_py(params$trees[[1]]) # get data into sklearn's preferred format y_idx <- ncol(analysis_set) - 1 X_idx <- y_idx - 1 pAnal <- r_to_py(analysis_set) y_train <- pAnal$iloc(axis = 1L)[y_idx]$values X_train <- pAnal$iloc(axis = 1L)[0:X_idx] model <- sklearn_e$RandomForestRegressor(criterion = "mae", max_features = max_features, n_estimators = n_estimators, random_state = 1L) mod_fit <- model$fit(X_train, y_train) } rf_params <- grid_latin_hypercube( mtry(range = c(3, 4)), trees(range = c(200, 300)), size = 40 ) is_sklearn <- function(modfun) { string <- toString(body(modfun)) stringr::str_detect(string, pattern = "sklearn") } # inputs params, model, and resample, calls model and error functions, outputs error mod_error <- function(params, mod_FUN, dat) { y_col <- ncol(dat$data) y_obs <- assessment(dat)[y_col] mod <- mod_FUN(params, analysis(dat)) if(is_sklearn(mod_FUN)) { X_dat <- r_to_py(assessment(dat)[-y_col]) pred <- mod$predict(X_dat) } else { pred <- predict(mod, assessment(dat)) if (!is.data.frame(pred)) { pred <- pred$predictions } } error <- error_FUN(y_obs, pred) error } # inputs resample, loops hyperparam grid values to model/error function, collects error value for hyperparam combo tune_over_params <- function(dat, mod_FUN, params) { params$error <- map_dbl(1:nrow(params), function(row) { params <- params[row,] mod_error(params, mod_FUN, dat) }) params } # inputs and sends fold's resamples to tuning function, collects and averages fold's error for each hyperparameter combo summarize_tune_results <- function(dat, mod_FUN, params) { # Return row-bound tibble that has the 25 bootstrap results param_names <- names(params) future_map_dfr(dat$splits, tune_over_params, mod_FUN, params, .progress = TRUE) %>% lazy_dt(., key_by = param_names) %>% # For each value of the tuning parameter, compute the # average which is the inner bootstrap estimate. group_by_at(vars(param_names)) %>% summarize(mean_error = mean(error, na.rm = TRUE), n = length(error)) %>% as_tibble() } compare_algs <- function(mod_FUN, params, ncv_dat){ # tune models by grid searching on resamples in the inner loop (e.g. 5 repeats 10 folds = list of 50 tibbles with param and mean_error cols) tuning_results <- map(ncv_dat$inner_resamples, summarize_tune_results, mod_FUN, params) } mod_FUN_list_skrf <- list(sklearn_rf = sklearn_rf_FUN) params_list <- list(sklearn_rf = rf_params) algorithm_comparison_two_skrf <- map2(mod_FUN_list_skrf, params_list, compare_algs, ncv_dat_2) #> Progress: 100% Progress: 100% Progress: --------------------------------------------------- 100% #> Error in mod_FUN(params, analysis(dat)): object 'sklearn_e' not found #> Called from: signalConditions(obj, exclude = getOption("future.relay.immediate", "immediateCondition"), resignal = resignal, ...) ``` Created on 2020-02-04 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)

title: py_to_r() not working for functions
description:
It seems like we can't modify the 'convert' flag for a python function that was created with `convert = FALSE`. I've run into versions of this bug with `py_run_file(local = TRUE, convert = FALSE)` too, this is just a minimal example. 

``` r
Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = Sys.which("python3"))
library(reticulate)

py_seq <- py_eval("lambda x: list(range(int(x)))")
py_seq(3) # good 
#> [1] 0 1 2

py_seq <- py_eval("lambda x: list(range(int(x)))", convert = FALSE)

py_seq(3) # bug 1, would expect this to work and return an unconverted object
#> Error in py_seq(3): could not find function "py_seq"
py_seq$`__call__`(3)  # it is callable like this however
#> [0, 1, 2]

py_to_r(py_seq)(3) # bug 2, now the call works, but the returned object is not converted
#> [0, 1, 2]
```

<sup>Created on 2020-01-31 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

Have a good weekend!

title: XGBoost Not Importing in R Markdown
description:
I've been trying several approaches to loading Python's `xgboost` into an R Markdown Python chunk and have not been able to find a solution.

When loading in `xgboost` I get the `ModuleNotFound` error

{python} chunk
`
import xgboost as xgb
`

I decided to look into where the `xgboost` module was installed and where `reticulate`'s Python was installed and found a mismatch. `reticulate` creates a new environment with Python 3.8.1 where `xgboost` did not get copied over. I tried installing `xgboost` in this environment but can't find examples of anyone doing so and wonder if 3.8.1 is even able to use `xgboost`. However, when trying to use the version of Python where `xgboost` is (3.7.6) I still had no luck. I even tried loading in Python's `xgboost` via R with `reticulate` but got the same error as above. This all can be seen in the image below:

![no_xgboost](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19579908/73386532-3af1c800-428c-11ea-9a32-b52f7679b488.PNG)

Now here's the kicker...when I knit the R markdown document it seems to run this just fine:

{r} chunk:
`
xgb <- reticulate::import('xgboost')
`

How can I get Python's version of `xgboost` to work interactively in R Markdown? Am I approaching this the wrong way or is there truly a bug? After searching the internet for this issue it looks like no one else is having a problem so I'm assuming this is a problem in approach.

title: Should /opt/... be added to search locations for find_conda()?
description:
Hi,

When running `R` in `RStudio`, my `R` session is unable to "automatically" find the conda binary in order to manage conda environments when using `reticulate`. It works when I explicitly provide the path to the conda binary (or when I run `R` from a shell external to `RStudio`), but I was wondering why it couldn't find conda since I installed anaconda in a pretty standard manner. Running `Sys.which('conda')` turns up nothing, meanwhile running `which conda` in the `RStudio` terminal finds the binary (probably because it searches `PATH`). Does `Sys.which()` not have access to `PATH`? It must not (at least in my case).

I went looking through the source code and noticed that `reticulate:::find_conda()` searches in a lot of standard locations, as shown below. However, as it turns out, my conda binary is located at `/opt/anaconda3/bin/conda`. Is this an unusual location? I'm sure I installed Anaconda in a "normal" way, so I'm wondering if `/opt/...` should be added to `conda_locations` in the below code, in addition to `~/opt/...` and others. For added context, I am on MacOS 10.14.6.

Happy to do submit a simple PR if you agree these paths should be added.

```r
find_conda <- function() {
  conda <- Sys.which("conda")
  if (!nzchar(conda)) {
    conda_locations <- c(
      miniconda_conda(),
      path.expand("~/opt/anaconda/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/opt/anaconda2/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/opt/anaconda3/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/opt/anaconda4/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/opt/miniconda/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/opt/miniconda2/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/opt/miniconda3/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/opt/miniconda4/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/anaconda/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/anaconda2/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/anaconda3/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/anaconda4/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/miniconda/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/miniconda2/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/miniconda3/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("~/miniconda4/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("/anaconda/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("/anaconda2/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("/anaconda3/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("/anaconda4/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("/miniconda/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("/miniconda2/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("/miniconda3/bin/conda"),
      path.expand("/miniconda4/bin/conda")
    )
    if (is_windows()) {
      anaconda_versions <- windows_registry_anaconda_versions()
      anaconda_versions <- subset(anaconda_versions, anaconda_versions$arch == .Platform$r_arch)
      if (nrow(anaconda_versions) > 0) {
        conda_scripts <- utils::shortPathName(
          file.path(anaconda_versions$install_path, "Scripts", "conda.exe")
        )
        conda_bats <- utils::shortPathName(
          file.path(anaconda_versions$install_path, "condabin", "conda.bat")
        )
        conda_locations <- c(conda_locations, conda_bats, conda_scripts)
      }
    }
    conda_locations <- conda_locations[file.exists(conda_locations)]
    if (length(conda_locations) > 0)
      conda_locations
    else
      NULL
  } else {
    conda
  }
}
```

title: Printing is deferred in RStudio
description:
If I run the following code in RStudio:

```r
library(reticulate)
builtins <- import_builtins()
builtins$print("foo")
```

I get no output. However, if I run it from an R terminal, I get the expected output:

```
foo
```

Note that in RStudio, if I later trigger anything in Python with reticulate (even running an empty Python command)

```r
library(reticulate)
builtins <- import_builtins()
builtins$print("foo")
# do some other stuff...
py_run_string("")
```

I will finally see the printed output:

```
foo
```

This is a critical issue in that for Python packages that print messages for the user, a user using RStudio will likely never see the messages, and if they do, it will not be at the time the message was intended to be printed.

title: Offer a full portable mode for install_miniconda
description:
While trying the last CRAN version 1.14 on my windows 10 work computer where I did not have admin right, `install_miniconda` prompte me with a box where I need to put an admin credential, which I don't have. I clicked "cancel" twice on the two prompts that opened, and that did the trick. Strange thing is I tried to reproduce but it did not prompt me again using the same command
```r
reticulate::install_miniconda(force = TRUE)
```

Anyway I wanted to share this because I believe the silent installation in `install_miniconda` does not apply a full portable installation and a portable installation mode could be insteresting. I did a little search. 

Here are the flags currently used: 
https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/43a27fd58310c277ac01e4f315958a1118c920b2/R/miniconda.R#L114-L123

Specifically, there is a `/AddToPath` flag that default to 1 (from the [silent mode doc](https://docs.anaconda.com/anaconda/install/silent-mode/)).  I think it tries to append to system PATH which is not possible. It could maybe write to user environment variable but it does not seem to be the case because I don't get anything in PATH regarding miniconda installation while `/AddToPath=1` by default. I think a portable installation mode could benefit from `/AddToPath=0`, leaving the user adding to PATH or not.

Also, currently, miniconda installation will write to registry. I think a full portable installation should not. There is a hidden flag about registry to no write to it; `/NoRegistry=1`. Look at the options through `.\Miniconda3-latest-Windows-x86_64.exe /?` an this thread https://github.com/conda/conda/issues/1977. Full portable mode could benefit from a `/NoRegistry=1` option for a clean portable installation.

Miniconda installer offers this full portable mode I think `install_miniconda` could use this, mainly for constraint environment, either by default or by a portable option 
```r
install_miniconda(..., portable = TRUE)
```

What do you think ?

title: conda_list cannot search specified path properly, conda_binary cannot test path properly
description:
I used rminiconda to install a miniconda, then hope to register the conda location with reticulate and use reticulate conda_ functions to install conda packages.

After setting `RETICULATE_MINICONDA_PATH` properly, conda_list can find it with auto option, but I want to specify it because there are multiple conda installations and the order is not guaranteed.

```r
> Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_MINICONDA_PATH = file.path(rminiconda::get_miniconda_path(), "gee"))
> reticulate:::miniconda_exists()
[1] TRUE
> conda_list()
  name                                          python
1  gee /Users/xhdong/Library/rminiconda/gee/bin/python
2  3.6      /Users/xhdong/anaconda/envs/3.6/bin/python
3 py27     /Users/xhdong/anaconda/envs/py27/bin/python
```

Then I tried to feed the conda location to conda_list to test it, then later use it to specify which conda to be used. However all kinds of variations cannot get it listed properly

```r
> conda_list("/Users/xhdong/Library/rminiconda/gee")
[1] name   python
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
> conda_list("/Users/xhdong/Library/rminiconda")
[1] name   python
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
> conda_list("/Users/xhdong/Library/rminiconda/gee/bin")
[1] name   python
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
# check conda_binary, which doesn't give any meaningful result
> reticulate:::conda_binary("/Users/xhdong/Library/rminiconda/gee")
[1] "/Users/xhdong/Library/rminiconda/gee"
> reticulate:::conda_binary("/Users/xhdong/Library/rminiconda")
[1] "/Users/xhdong/Library/rminiconda"
```

I tracked and found [`conda_binary` logic have some missing cases](https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/master/R/conda.R#L234)

```r
altpath <- file.path(dirname(conda), "../bin/conda")
```
- line above try to go out of user provided path one step up, then go down one step down to bin to look for conda. 
- However dirname already provided a parent folder, so the altpath created will not find bin/conda, thus altpath is non-exist.
- Worse, the program leave this condition branch, but just test if the original path exist and return that path to be the conda binary path. 
   I'm not sure what's the case is expected here. If conda should always be either in bin/conda or condabin/conda.bat, is there any other valid case other than these two? line 244-250 means if a path didn't pass previous logic but exist, it will be reported as a valid conda binary.
   Here I think there is a confusion: is the function expecting the folder of conda exe (xx/bin), or the full path of conda executable (xx/bin/conda)? Normally user would expect the former, then just testing path exist doesn't really test if conda binary exist.

In summary
- `..` in line 234 should be removed
- the logic between 244-250 might need to be fully removed, other than an error report. 

@kevinushey , I'd love to create a PR if needed.

title: Struggling to make reticulate Python REPL run tabbed code
description:
I love reticulate and using Python in RStudio - thank you so much. 

I'm running into this problem when opening in RStudio a python file which was written somewhere else, say Notepad++, and the code is tabbed (say after a for loop statement, after an empty line or after a function def statement),  and I want to run it interactively (selecting a bunch of lines and using Ctrl+Enter).

The problem is that the REPL won't recognize that the tabbed lines (after the first tabbed line) are continuing the loop/def. As if the loop/def finished and the script continues. The IDLE REPL or Pycharm REPL do not do that, I checked.

Example 1:
```python
for i in range(3):
	print(i)
	print(i + 1)
```
(where those print statements need to be tabbed or copy pasted from, say, Notepad++, not written in R editor)

If you COPY-PASTE this in the REPL you get:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9554580/71106727-819dce00-21c8-11ea-9b5c-6a3ba317a3d8.png)

Which obviously won't do what you want. And again copying-pasting in IDLE or PyCharm works fine.

Example 2:
```python
for i in range(3):
	print(i)

	print(i + 1)
```
(where between the first and second print statements there is an EMPTY line, not a tabbed empty line)
Copy-paste this in the R editor, then select and do Ctrl + Enter.

You get:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9554580/71107086-26201000-21c9-11ea-9b19-d9cdd6363906.png)

Which obviously won't do what you want. The difference between Example 1 and Example 2 is that Example 1 *will* work with Ctrl + Enter, but not Example 2. And again, Example 2 also works with IDLE/Pycharm. And of course works if put say in a main function and run with `python test.py` wherever, including `py_run_file()` in R.

This may seem petty, but imagine you are learning a subject in Python, you get a bunch of scripts you would like to run interactively, they are written this way, and before every run you have to fix the empty lines like in Example 2. So either there are no empty lines or there is also a tab.

title: should install_miniconda() by default install into the default installation directory?
description:
When installing Anaconda on macOS Catalina using the GUI installer tool (not reticulate), the default installation location is in `~/opt` according to this [documentation](https://docs.anaconda.com/anaconda/install/mac-os/#installing-on-macos). In #661, the proposal to look in this directory for the binary was accepted. I believe the default for installing Miniconda with `reticulate::install_miniconda(..., path = miniconda_path())` should be the same as the default installation path when using the official installer (at least this would be a reasonable expectation), so on macOS, it should not be `~/Librar/r-miniconda`, but `~/opt` (at least for macOS Catalina). Otherwise, the Miniconda installation can't actually be used by `reticulate::conda_install()` and potentially others I believe because `~/Librar/r-miniconda` is again not listed in `reticulate:::find_conda()` as described in #661. The same logic applies to other operating systems like Linux and Windows.

This boils down to adapting `miniconda_path()` to return these default paths. Does this sound reasonable?

cc: @hafen

title: Conda binary not found on macOS due to changed installation location
description:
When installing Anaconda on macOS Catalina, the default installation location is in `~/opt` according to this [documentation](https://docs.anaconda.com/anaconda/install/mac-os/#installing-on-macos). My experience is that this is also where Miniconda is installed. However, previous versions of macOS would install conda elsewhere, so `reticulate::conda_binary()` won't find it, because `reticulate:::find_conda()`does not look in `~/opt` apparently. So I get this:

```r
reticulate::conda_binary()
#> Error: Unable to find conda binary. Is Anaconda installed?
```

I think this can be fixed by adding simply adding these path to `conda_locations` in [`reticulate:::find_conda()`](https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/92e03419e49f39bf2c350e764f91816bb47ced47/R/conda.R#L293).

Happens with `tensorflow==2.0.0b1` and `tensorflow==1.15`, as well as both github and CRAN versions of reticulate, keras, and tensorflow R pkgs. 

Code to reproduce:
```{R}
library(keras)

keras_model_simple_mlp <- function(num_classes, 
                                   use_bn = FALSE, use_dp = FALSE, 
                                   name = NULL) {
  
  # define and return a custom model
  keras_model_custom(name = name, function(self) {
    
    # create layers we'll need for the call (this code executes once)
    self$dense1 <- layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "relu")
    self$dense2 <- layer_dense(units = num_classes, activation = "softmax")
    if (use_dp)
      self$dp <- layer_dropout(rate = 0.5)
    if (use_bn)
      self$bn <- layer_batch_normalization(axis = -1)
    
    # implement call (this code executes during training & inference)
    function(inputs, mask = NULL) {
      x <- self$dense1(inputs)
      if (use_dp)

      if (use_bn)

      self$dense2(x)
    }
  })

description:
Hi,

I am trying to do KNN classification in R calling the K nearest neighbors classifier from sklearn.

Here's the function

```
SKLEARN_NEIGHBORS <- reticulate::import('sklearn.neighbors')
MODEL_SELECTION <- reticulate::import('sklearn.model_selection')
METRICS <- reticulate::import('sklearn.metrics')

fit_knn_cv <- function(X, y, k_vals = 3:20) {
  ## Fit KNN classifier with 5 fold CV
  ## INPUTS:
  ##  X = input data
  ##  y = class labels
  ##  k_vals = range of k values to test
  ## OUTPUTS:
  ##  model fit with best performing value of k, as well as average 
  
  cv_avg <- c()
  cv_sdev <- c()
  for (k in k_vals) {
    knn_model <- SKLEARN_NEIGHBORS$KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors = k, metric = 'minkowski', p = 2L)
    cv_scores <- MODEL_SELECTION$cross_val_score(estimator = knn_model, X = X, y = y, cv = 5L, scoring = 'accuracy')
    cv_avg <- c(cv_avg, mean(cv_scores))
    cv_sdev <- c(cv_sdev, sd(cv_scores))
  }
  # take value of k with maximum CV score average. break ties by taking smaller value k
  k_select <- k_vals[which(cv_avg == max(cv_avg))]
  model_output<- SKLEARN_NEIGHBORS$KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors = k_select, metric = 'minkowski', p = 2)

  return(output)
}

title: Python 3.8 no longer uses libpython - (sorry my bad, build python 3.8 with configure --enable-shared and reticulate works)
description:
Hi,
I have installed Python 3.8 as an alternate installation on Ubuntu 18.04 (under /opt/Python-3.8.0).  The system is still able to use the default Python that came with Ubuntu.

I created a virtual environment in my home directory with:
python -m venv tf38

I can not get python to initialize in R:

> library(reticulate)
> use_virtualenv("~/tf38")
> py_config()
Error in initialize_python(required_module, use_environment) :
  Python shared library not found, Python bindings not loaded.
> py_discover_config()
python:         /home/daniel/tf38/bin/python
libpython:      [NOT FOUND]
pythonhome:     /usr/local:/usr/local
version:        3.8.0 (default, Oct 20 2019, 16:51:39)  [GCC 7.4.0]
numpy:          /home/daniel/tf38/lib/python3.8/site-packages/numpy
numpy_version:  1.17.3
 
I believe this is because Python 3.8 no longer uses libpython (the file is not included and can not be installed).  

I believe this is relevant (from https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.8.html):

"On Unix, C extensions are no longer linked to libpython except on Android and Cygwin. When Python is embedded, libpython must not be loaded with RTLD_LOCAL, but RTLD_GLOBAL instead. Previously, using RTLD_LOCAL, it was already not possible to load C extensions which were not linked to libpython, like C extensions of the standard library built by the *shared* section of Modules/Setup. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in bpo-21536.)"

Please patch reticulate() to work with Python 3.8 and Python 3.8 virtual environments which are without libpython.

Many thanks,
Daniel

title: py_config reports twice the same versions on windows
description:
While discovering the new dev version of reticulate with the use of miniconda, I just stumble upon what I think to be an unwanted behavior on windows. 

## Behavior

`py_config` and `py_discover` just reports twice the same python version because it does not get correctly deduplicated as some path are using `/` and others `\\`

``` r
reticulate::py_config()
#> python:         C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/r-miniconda/envs/r-reticulate/python.exe
#> libpython:      C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/r-miniconda/envs/r-reticulate/python36.dll
#> pythonhome:     C:\Users\chris\AppData\Local\r-miniconda\envs\r-reticulate
#> version:        3.6.9 |Anaconda, Inc.| (default, Jul 30 2019, 14:00:49) [MSC v.1915 64 bit (AMD64)]
#> Architecture:   64bit
#> numpy:          C:\Users\chris\AppData\Local\r-miniconda\envs\r-reticulate\lib\site-packages\numpy
#> numpy_version:  1.16.5
#> 
#> python versions found: 
#>  C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/r-miniconda/envs/r-reticulate/python.exe
#>  C:\Users\chris\AppData\Local\r-miniconda\envs\r-reticulate\python.exe
#>  C:\Users\chris\AppData\Local\r-miniconda\python.exe
```

We see that first and second versions are the same. 
Also, path form different components are returned sometime with `/` and sometimes with `\`.

Let's clarify that everything is working fine then, but I wonder if this should be change or not.

## Analysis

One is found looking a miniconda envpath
``` r
reticulate:::miniconda_envpath("r-reticulate")
#> [1] "C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/r-miniconda/envs/r-reticulate"
reticulate::miniconda_path()
#> [1] "C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/r-miniconda"
```

but it explicitly normalizing path with `/`:
https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/565ba8f117f5fefd0a1038a522411b2cf2128e27/R/miniconda.R#L158

Whereas others versions are reported by conda using `\\`
``` r
reticulate:::python_conda_versions()
#>           name
#> 1  r-miniconda
#> 2 r-reticulate
#>                                                                          python
#> 1                     C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\r-miniconda\\python.exe
#> 2 C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\r-miniconda\\envs\\r-reticulate\\python.exe
```

The third is reported by
``` r
reticulate:::py_versions_windows()
#>       type hive                                  install_path
#> 1 Anaconda  HCU C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\r-miniconda
#>                                             executable_path version arch
#> 1 C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\r-miniconda\\python.exe     3.7  x64
```

Two of them only should be kept when de-duplication happens
https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/565ba8f117f5fefd0a1038a522411b2cf2128e27/R/config.R#L214-L215

`/` and `\` gets mixed up when printing `py_config` result. It would benefit to be more consitent I guess.

title: TypeError when passing an argument to a Python function using reticulate
description:
This is a problem that was first posted at Stackoverflow [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58082690/typeerror-when-using-reticulate-package-to-call-a-function-from-python-peakutils) and has been met with resounding silence for almost a fortnight, so I thought I'd try here.

I'm trying to use the Python function `indexes` from the package `peakutils`. The code below works fine.

```
# Load packages
library(data.table)
library(reticulate)

# Set RNG
set.seed(-1)

# Synthetic data function
foo <- function(x) sin(x) * sqrt(x) + rnorm(length(x), 0, 0.1)

# Create data
dt <- data.table(x = seq(0, 10, by = 0.1))
dt$y <- foo(dt$x)

# Import Python library
pu <- import("peakutils")

# Indices pf peaks
ind <- pu$indexes(dt$y, thres = 0.7)
```

Now, when I try to include the argument `min_dist` I get an error:

```
# Indices pf peaks now with a larger minimum distance
ind <- pu$indexes(dt$y, thres = 0.7, min_dist = 3L)
```

> Error in py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords) :
> TypeError: only integer arrays with one element can be converted to an index

It seems like `3L` – and integer array with only one element – is not being recognised as such. Am I passing the argument incorrectly or is something else amiss?

title: use_condaenv() does not throw error when the specified environment is not present
description:
Hi,

`use_condaenv("xxx", required = TRUE)` throws error if the environment `xxx` is not available whereas `use_condaenv("xxx") does not throw any error if the environment `xxx` is not available.

I think `required=TRUE` should be the default when using conda or virtualenv. It may not be necessary for python. Also, adding this information in documentation will help.

title: supply np record array from R
description:
Hello, 
I would like to use the [multimatch module](https://pypi.org/project/multimatch/), but I mainly work in R with Rstudio. In order to use the `doComparison()` function, I need to supply the input data (a nx3 array) as a "record array" (at least that's what the developers of the module do in their [example](https://multimatch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html)).
But R complains about unexpected parenthesis or commas, for example in: `fix_vector1 = np$recfromcsv('MYPATH/MMtrial1.tsv', delimiter='\t', dtype= {'names': ('start_x', 'start_y', 'duration'), 'formats': ('f8', 'f8', 'f8')})`. But it does also complain about unexpected brackets in this: `a = np_array([(1,'ABC'), (2, "DEF")], dtype=[('foo', int), ('bar', 'S4')])`

So my question is: (how) can I supply the record array to the `doComparison()` function? And in general: how does reticulate deal with python arrays that do not only contain numbers and that use bracket differently than how they are used in R?

I have tried to supply `doComparison()` with an R list, matrix, data.frame and tibble of the data without success and I can't imagine what else could be interpreted as a record array. 

Thank you for your help!

Lilla

links on record arrays:
Here is the documentation of structured arrays in [python](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/numpy/user/basics.rec.html)
Here are examples of how other people used the [np.recfromcsv](https://www.programcreek.com/python/example/18482/numpy.recarray)

title: install_tensorflow "hybrid" result with conda on linux (and the default conda entries in .bashrc)
description:
Sorry  for resurgitating the installation topic :-)

Opening this here because `install_tensorflow` delegates most all of the logic to `py_install`.

I just noticed that on linux, the following can happen when you have allowed `conda` to add their initialization code to `bashrc`:

```
# >>> conda initialize >>>
# !! Contents within this block are managed by 'conda init' !!
__conda_setup="$('/home/key/anaconda3/bin/conda' 'shell.bash' 'hook' 2> /dev/null)"
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    eval "$__conda_setup"
else
    if [ -f "/home/key/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh" ]; then
        . "/home/key/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh"
    else
        export PATH="/home/key/anaconda3/bin:$PATH"
    fi
fi
unset __conda_setup
# <<< conda initialize <<<

```
As a result of this, Anaconda's `base` env python is always on the `PATH`:

```
(base) [key@snowi ~]$ echo $PATH 
/home/key/anaconda3/bin:/home/key/anaconda3/condabin:/home/key/.local/bin:/home/key/bin:/usr/share/Modules/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/bin:/usr/sbin

```

Now when I start RStudio and do

```
tensorflow::install_tensorflow("")
```

I get a virtualenv based on - as it looks like - the alphabetically first environment `conda` knows (which would be `1.14`):

```py_config()

title: Issue with python sysconfig in reticulate:::python_config()
description:
I'm using miniconda3 and python 3.7 and am running into an issue when using `reticulate::import()`. I've traced it back to an issue that happens in `reticulate:::python_config()`, specifically the line 
``` 
config <- system2(command = python, args = paste0("\"", config_script, 
        "\""), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)
```
To wit, the issue is with python, so feel free to stop reading here. It seems that when sourcing the python config script, the first `sysconfig` command after the import results in the string `4.8.5-16)` as well as a couple newlines getting printed to stdout, which in this case gets appended to the previous line. The previous line happens to be the VersionNumber line, so this results in a VersionNumber of `3.74.8.5-16)` when really it should just be `3.7`. The final result is the error
```
Error: invalid version specification ‘NA’
```
or, if I alter the code to avoid `NA` values in the output of the `read.dcf()` command, the error
```
Error: invalid version specification ‘3.74.8.5-16)’

I'm curious if anyone else is running into this. I'll keep digging and file a bug report somewhere closer to the root of the problem at any rate.

```
library(reticulate)

[[2]]
<class 'list'>

[[3]]
<class 'list'>

title: ParamValidationError when trying to pass NULL or NA for optional parameter
description:
I'm writing an R package ([`pyMTurkR`](https://github.com/cloudyr/pyMTurkR/)) that uses [`reticulate`](https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate) to wrap around the [boto3 python SDK](https://github.com/boto/boto3/tree/develop/boto3). 

I'm running into problems when trying to write a wrapper to a python function that has optional parameters. I'd like to be able to pass `NULL` or `NA` to the python client in R, but since the python function is expecting a value for these parameters (despite what the SDK says), it's returning an error.

For example, in R I have the following code:

```
boto3 <- reticulate::import("boto3")
client <- boto3$client('mturk', region_name='us-east-1',
                                    aws_access_key_id = key,
                                    aws_secret_access_key = secret_key,
                                    endpoint_url = endpoint_url)
client$list_hits(MaxResults = NULL)
```

`MaxResults` is, according to the python SDK documents, an optional parameter. But the function will only run if `MaxResults` is not passed as a parameter, or if an integer value is given. The code above returns an error with parameter validation: `ParamValidationError: Parameter validation failed`. 

Traceback below:

```
Error in py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords) : 
  ParamValidationError: Parameter validation failed:
Invalid type for parameter MaxResults, value: None, type: <class 'NoneType'>, valid types: <class 'int'> 
2. stop(structure(list(message = "ParamValidationError: Parameter validation failed:\nInvalid type for parameter MaxResults, value: None, type: <class 'NoneType'>, valid types: <class 'int'>", 
    call = py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords), 
    cppstack = structure(list(file = "", line = -1L, stack = "C++ stack not available on this system"), class = "Rcpp_stack_trace")), class = c("Rcpp::exception", 
"C++Error", "error", "condition"))) 
1. client$list_hits(MaxResults = NULL) 
```

I've managed to work around this by building up the function call as a string, with conditional `paste()` for the optional parameters, that I later `eval(parse())`. For example

```
request <- "client$list_hits("
if(!is.null(maxresults)) {
      request <- paste0(request, "MaxResults = as.integer(", maxresults, ")")
}
request <- paste0(request, ")")
eval(parse(text = request))
```

Now, using `eval(parse())` wouldn't ordinarily be a big problem, but some of the parameters that the python function is expecting are nested dictionary objects, and the only way I've managed to get those to pass is by using _nested_ calls to `eval(parse())`. This is obviously leading to some pretty bad (albeit functional) R programming.

I might be missing something, but it seems like my problems would go away if only reticulate could handle NULL/NA parameters gracefully (e.g., not pass them along to python). Is this possible? Am I missing something obvious about optional parameters? Or should I try talking to `boto3` developers to see if a fix can be put in on the python side?

Thanks.

Hi there, I'm having difficulties calling python code from my shiny app after I have deployed it to a unix server. The app calls an Adobe API in Python and from the filters I provide the user in a Shiny app. When the data is returned, it's displayed in a DT table.

This application works fine on my local machine. The python environment being loaded is from a virtual environment. On the server, here is the information of the virtual environment:

```
> source .venv/bin/activate
> python --version
Python 3.6.5 :: Anaconda, Inc.
```

```
> cat requirements.txt
certifi==2019.6.16
chardet==3.0.4
future==0.17.1
idna==2.8
numpy==1.16.4
git+http://github.com/dancingcactus/python-omniture.git
pandas==0.25.0
python-dateutil==2.8.0
pytz==2019.1
requests==2.22.0
six==1.12.0
urllib3==1.25.3
```
In my R code, I have: `Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = '.venv/bin/python')`

My app loads perfectly fine. However, when I click the submit button (where the Python logic is at), it immediately breaks and throws this error:

```
 *** caught segfault ***
address (nil), cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: py_call_impl(callable, dots$args, dots$keywords)
 2: get_omniture_analytics()

 4: ..stacktraceon..(`<reactive:omniture_analytics>`(...))
 5: .func()

10: force(expr)
11: globals$domain$wrapSync(expr)

16: ctx$run(function() {    result <- withCallingHandlers({        .error <<- FALSE        withVisible(.func())    }, error = function(cond) {        .value <<- cond        .error <<- TRUE        .visible <<- $
17: self$.updateValue()

```

The `get_omniture_analytics` function calls an authenticate method from the `omniture` module in python. It looks really similar to this:
```
def get_omniture_analytics():
    analytics = omniture.authenticate('my_username', 'my_secret')

```
More information regarding this module can be found here: https://github.com/dancingcactus/python-omniture

I've seen these segfault errors popping up from time to time, but it usually involves heavier computations like Keras and/or tensorflow. I haven't found many examples that throw segfaults without calling those libraries. Any thoughts on this?

title: S4 Class with Python object in slots
description:
I'm fairly new to R and have an issue when creating a S4 class.

What I have is a Python wrapper class that is used with reticulate in order to gain access to our Python API. This works perfectly when manually calling it in the console. 

I am now trying to create a thin wrapper in R that helps the users use the Python API without actually knowing that they are using Python at all. 

The class will be used by all R users of our application so that they can send data from their R workspace to our application and work with it. 

The problem is now that I do not know how to correctly setup a class with the returned Python instance of my Python class.

`> class(inst)`
`[1] "python.builtin.module" "python.builtin.object"`

This instance would be created upon calling the constructor of my class and be stored in the slot. However, I am unsure how to proceed to find out how to correctly define my slot

currently my setClass looks as follows:
`apihelper<-setClass("apihelper",
           slots=c(handle="python.builtin.object"))`

Currently I receive this warning upon loading my package:
`Warning: undefined slot classes in definition of "apihelper": handle(class "python.builtin.object")`

and when calling the constructor I receive this error:
` Error in validObject(.Object) : 
  invalid class “apihelper” object: undefined class for slot "handle" ("python.builtin.object") `

I know that the handle definition is obviously wrong, but I do not know how to correctly define it so that I can work with the reticulate object.

Is there a way to determine the correct class string? Or is this even possible with reticulate?

#Traceback:
#1. adata$obsm[["velocity_umap"]]
#2. `[[.python.builtin.object`(adata$obsm, "velocity_umap")
#3. py_get_attr_or_item(x, name, TRUE)
#4. py_get_attr(x, name)

> adata$obsm['velocity_umap']
#Error in as.environment(x): invalid 'pos' argument

#1. adata$obsm["velocity_umap"]
#2. `[.python.builtin.object`(adata$obsm, "velocity_umap")

> adata$obsm$`__getitem__`('velocity_umap')
#2×540 matrix

```

`` `[[.python.builtin.object` `` calls `py_get_attr_or_item(..., prefer_attr = TRUE)`, and with `prefer_attr = TRUE`, it doesn’t even try to access an item.

Calling ``myobj$`__getitem__`('key')`` isn’t really acceptable, and I don’t think dicts should get special treatment here anyway, but rely on the default behavior

title: use `reticulate` with debug-enabled Python
description:
Using `reticulate` with a debug-enabled Python throws

```Error in py_initialize(config$python, config$libpython, config$pythonhome,  :
 PyModule_Create2 - /home/key/python/python3.7/lib/libpython3.7m.so: undefined symbol: PyModule_Create2
```

The reason is that what's `PyModule_Create2` in "normal" Python is  `PyModule_Create2TraceRefs` in debug-enabled Python (cf. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39161202/how-to-work-around-missing-pymodule-create2-in-amd64-win-python35-d-lib).

Simply replacing all 3 occurrences does not work though, as a `tf_config` now results in 

```
*** caught segfault ***
address (nil), cause 'unknown'

Traceback:
1: py_run_string_impl(paste0("import sys; sys.path.append('", system.file("python",     package = "reticulate"), "')"))
2: initialize_python(required_module, use_environment)
3: ensure_python_initialized(required_module = module)
4: import(module)
5: doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler)
6: tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
7: tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)

title: Reticulate takes over python path
description:
Minimum reproducible example:

```
require(reticulate)

Sys.which("python3")
os = import("os", as = "os", delay_load = FALSE)
os$listdir("./")
Sys.which("python3")
```

At first, system calls will say that python3 is found in `/usr/local/bin/python3`. However, after reticulate is loaded and python is initialized, a second system call says python3 is found in `/usr/bin/python3`.  This is confusing, because the system call has nothing to do with reticulate and I should still be able to use it, but reticulate has contaminated it. Depending on the order of my calls I could get different, or broken behavior. 

The offending logic begins in `python_config` [here](https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/35da856f60ac7f8dc7c2da120e07df881b4f3606/R/config.R#L343). The exact calls are

`import` -> `ensure_python_initialized` -> `initialize_python` -> `py_discover_config` -> `python_config` -> `python_munge_path` -> `path_prepend`, which finally sets an environment variable. Ideally the environment variable would be restored after python_config is done. I think...though I'm not certain...there is some kind of logic meant to restore the old path [here](https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/35da856f60ac7f8dc7c2da120e07df881b4f3606/R/config.R#L347) but the logic can't be correct. When it adds on.exit, the path has already been "munged", meaning it was already converted from the original `/usr/local/bin/python` to `/usr/bin` and thus would restore my environment variables to find python3 in `/usr/bin/python3`. 

I understand I can force a particular python path using `use_python`, which would not contaminate any environment variables. However, that solution is very subtle, and difficult to share with teammates. Can this be addressed more elegantly by resolving the on.exit issue?

title: Error: C stack usage  (big number) is too close to the limit
description:
Trying to run a custom generator function with multithreading  on Ubuntu 18.04 with a simple keras (version 2.2.4) model and reticulate (version 1.10), I get random `Error: C stack usage 459557818812 is too close to the limit` errors and some threads crash.

```
def run_model(test_set, validation_set, epochs, workers, use_multiprocessing):
    model = keras.models.Sequential()
    model.add(keras.layers.Dense(units = 50, activation = "relu", input_shape = (10,100)))
    model.add(keras.layers.Dropout(rate=0.2))
    model.add(keras.layers.Dense(units=2,activation="softmax"))
    model.compile(loss = "categorical_crossentropy",optimizer = "rmsprop",metrics =["accuracy"])
    g_train = MySequenceClass(test_set)
    g_valid = MySequenceClass(validation_set)
    model.fit_generator(generator=g_train, validation_data=g_valid, epochs=epochs, workers=workers, use_multiprocessing=use_multiprocessing)
```

A similar closed issue #288 says it was a bug in OP's code. I am not so sure:
- the threads don't crash with use_multiprocessing=FALSE
- the threads don't crash when run from python on the same data
- the threads crash via reticulate with any sensible values of linux stack limit, however
- the threads *don't crash* when I set `ulimit -s unlimited` and run via reticulate
- R crashes randomly when I try to define a custom generator in R and use R's `keras` package with `use_multithreading=TRUE`. 
- the numbers reported, like `459557818812` are way above my available RAM, and they look more like a bug in R's stack calculation when using multithreading?

(I am sorry, but I do not have time at the moment to provide a complete self-contained example.)

title: `caught segfault, cause 'memory not mapped'` after calling reticulate functions on NixOS
description:
I'm attempting to use Reticulate (via keras/tensorflow) on NixOS and running into a segfault.

Nix has it's own way of doing things involving a centralized store of binaries that are then referenced in user environments via symlinks, meaning a lot of tools used to construct environments like virtualenv fail since the binaries are not explicitly where the tools are expected. In this case I am able to drop into a `nix-shell` as outlined in heading [9.14.1.1.3.1](https://nixos.org/nixpkgs/manual/#using-python) that has python, keras, and tensorflow available. I can successfully launch a python REPL from this shell and import/assign keras objects. 

I can also launch an R REPL and load reticulate, but attempting to use any reticulate functions causes the following segfault and traceback:

```
*** caught segfault ***
address 0x8, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: py_run_string_impl(paste0("import sys; sys.path.append('", system.file("python",     package = "reticulate"), "')"))
 2: initialize_python(required_module, use_environment)
 3: ensure_python_initialized()
 4: import_builtins(convert = FALSE)
 5: repl_python()
```

R is aware of python's and reticulate's location in the nix-store:

```
> Sys.which('python')
                                                                    python 
"/nix/store/m2br92794yw09hjwh3vzadbphckagmzv-python3-3.7.3-env/bin/python" 

> paste0("import sys; sys.path.append('", system.file("python",     package = "reticulate"), "')")
[1] "import sys; sys.path.append('/nix/store/v64aywkbbr4qj92xv19fxmhdv66icl3q-r-reticulate-1.10/library/reticulate/python')"
```

This appears to be some kind of error with how reticulate is calling `py_run_string_impl`. It may be that I have more work to do with pulling in the correct dependencies in a Nix-friendly way but I don't think a segfault is the appropriate way for this to fail.

title: use_virtualenv can't find venv/bin?
description:
Context: On OSX with a virtualenv named "venv" and an anaconda installation in the background (outside of venv)

Problem: Importing my python module as `reticulate::import("mymodule")` was complaining about not being able to find matplotlib even after running `use_virtualenv("/Users/me/mypackage/venv")`. This problem occurred in Rstudio but did not occur from a terminal R session initiated inside of the activate virtual environment.

Temporary solution: Basically the same as suggested in https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/issues/367, which is to tell reticulate to look inside of venv/bin by updating the system PATH before loading the library:
```
vbin = "/Users/me/mypackage/venv/bin"
Sys.setenv(PATH= paste(vbin,Sys.getenv()["PATH"],sep=":"))
library(reticulate) 
```

title: `use_python()` should throw an error if Python is already embedded and the path doesn't match
description:
`use_python()` will silently succeed without having any effect if the session is already initialized and thus the path cannot be changed. The user typically has no control over whether Python has already been initialized or not (since any other package could have initialized it), so it is important to know if the requested path cannot be honored.

The most common pitfall is that some package initialized python2 and you need python3, but reticulate won't warn that you're not getting what you asked for (and thus nothing will work).

This was partially discussed in #418 but the answer there ("we'll find the version of Python you need") makes no sense to me since the whole issue is that you get the wrong version and won't know it.

title: R Studio numpy version
description:
Please refer to the following stack overflow message
`https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51541031/numpy-version-is-not-satisfied-for-tensorflow`
Error in py_dict_impl(keys, values, convert = convert) : Evaluation error: Required version of NumPy not available: installation of Numpy >= 1.6 not found
The issue seems to be here:
`# check numpy version and provide a load error message if we don't satisfy it
  if (is.null(config$numpy) || config$numpy$version < "1.6")
    numpy_load_error <- "installation of Numpy >= 1.6 not found"
  else`
Please note, that the version is found in R, there seems just to be a difficulty to interpret the version w/ 2 dots. Please see the follwing output from R
` np <- reticulate::import("numpy")
> print(np$version$full_version)
[1] "1.15.4"
> `

Hence there is **no** env/path issue!
I would compile a new version, if I would know, how to clone and compile in Windows for Windows 10. When I installed it, it did compile by itself (hence I have the necessary tools installed as cc, make etc. but I don't know, how to use them in windows.
Thanks

title: reticulate does not care about the environment
description:
## ~~reticulate does not care about the environment~~
... sorry for the hopefully click bait title ...

Several open issues, namely, #292, #311, #338, #396, https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/677 are caused by python loaded by reticulate from a conda environment not finding shared libraries which would be found by python started directly from that environment.  (leading to e.g. `ImportError: /usr/lib64/libstdc++.so.6: version 'CXXABI_1.3.9' not found`)

With this issue I hope to initiate a discussion on: 
## How should and how can reticulate handle the process environment & shared library search paths?

Here is what I think to understand about it:
* reticulate loads libpython => R and python live in the same process
* when loading python, reticulate modifies the environment a bit but not as much as `conda activate` would
* these modifications could cause issues for the rest of the R session (might add an incompatible gcc version etc)
* there is [this partial workaround for windows](https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/blob/8d1a668491ea89051721b8e06fb182cfd63647e0/R/package.R#L95)
* changing LD_LIBRARY_PATH of a running linux process has no effect
* the problem only surfaces if  the shared library versions are not available in the R environment (= always when using a HPC cluster, almost never when using your own up-to date machine )
* there could be silent errors
* probably the same points apply to virtualenv

My conclusion is:
* reticulate cannot use a different (virtual) environment than the R process it is running in :cry:
* `use_condaenv` cannot work (without starting a separate process which it never will) and should be removed/deprecated in favor of starting the R session in the adequate conda environment (having conda manage R as well would help to handle conflicts between R and python requirements)

What do you think?

title: No warning when use_* functions have no effect
description:
### Repro

1. Start a fresh R session.
2. Run `reticulate::use_python("/path/to/pythonA")`
3. Run `reticulate::py_run_string("print sys.version")`
4. Run `reticulate::use_python("/path/to/pythonB")`
5. Run `reticulate::py_run_string("print sys.version")`

### Observe

The Python version has not changed; the second `use_python()` directive has no effect, and the first Python version remains active.

### Expected

I ran into this while testing the reticulate behavior in R notebooks, wherein it seemed like `use_python` wasn't being respected (see https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/4130). It turns out that I'd been running a Python chunk (which implicitly loaded the default Python) before calling `use_python` -- too late; once a Python version is loaded, you can't change it without a restart. However, it took quite a bit of trial and error to discover why `use_python()` wasn't doing anything.

It seems like the `use_*` family should either: 

1. allow for switching at runtime between Pythons, perhaps with a warning/force flag so that, if Python is already loaded and differs from the requested version, the caller acknowledges that the session will be ended and state cleared in order to switch, or
2. emit a warning when trying to invoke the `use_*` family when Python is already loaded.

description:
### Versions:

R version: 3.5.1
Reticulate version: 1.10
Python version: 3.6.7

### Description:

When I run a Python script (image classifier with pytorch) via a Reticulated Rmd document, I get different results on my laptop vs. a Linux machine. On Mac, the model predictions are correct and consistent between runs. On Linux, the model predictions are random and incorrect. I can reproduce this random behavior using the steps below.

I was initially having this problem via a Reticulated Shiny app, but I transferred the code to an Rmd document and was able to reproduce the inconsistent behavior.

### Steps to reproduce:

Note that I configure the path to Python using the `use_python()` function in the Rmd example below whether I am running the document on Mac or Linux. On both the Mac and Linux machines, I am using the same versions of R, Python, and the same versions of the R and Python packages.

1) Create a Python environment on Mac machine with the packages listed in the `requirements.txt` below.
2) Run the below Rmd document on Mac and observe the resulting predictions, which remain the same if you re-run the document multiple times (see Expected Output). I used the following command:
   ```    
   R -e 'Sys.setenv(RSTUDIO_PANDOC="/Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/pandoc"); rmarkdown::render("image-classifier.Rmd")'
   ```
3) Create a Python environment on Linux machine with the packages listed in the `requirements.txt` below.
4) Run the same Rmd document on Linux. I used the following command:
   ```    
   /opt/R/3.5.1/bin/R -e 'Sys.setenv(RSTUDIO_PANDOC="/usr/lib/rstudio/bin/pandoc"); rmarkdown::render("image-classifier.Rmd")'
   ```
5) Observe very different resulting predictions each time you re-run the Rmd document on Linux (see Actual Output).

### Expected output:

Since the image URL is fixed, the classification model (`squeezenet1_1`) is fixed/pre-trained and downloaded to the`./model/` dir upon execution, and the model is initialized in evaluation/test mode using `sqnet.eval()`, thus the model should always return the same predictions.

With these fixed parameters, the output I always get on Mac is as follows (even when executing multiple times):

```

## tiger cat 30.400385
## tabby, tabby cat 29.59031
## lynx, catamount 29.143005
## hen 24.640438
```

### Actual output:

When I run the Rmd document on Linux, I get random results for the categories and scores. For example, when I run the Rmd document three times, I get the following random categories and scores:

```

Also note that the scores in the `predictions` array are many orders of magnitude higher than when I run the document on my Mac (see Expected Output).

### Files necessary to reproduce:
